1900.name: The Gate

north.description: To the north lies The Front Yard.

south.description: To the south lies The Field.

1900.description:
A tall gate of black wrought iron stands in an arch of crumbling brick,
one leaf hanging open on a single rusted hinge. A worn path leads out
through the grass toward the old cathedral's churchyard, and the smell
of turned earth drifts in on the draught. The way north runs on through
the arch to the front yard, between pillars topped with weathered stone
urns. A bell-pull dangles from its chain beside the gate, and it swings
a little though nothing touches it.

1901.name: The Front Yard

north.description: To the north lies The Grand Foyer.

south.description: To the south lies The Gate.

1901.description:
Weeds as high as your waist choke what was once a formal garden, and a
cracked gravel drive curls between them toward the house. A dry fountain
stands off to one side, its basin green with scum and its stone cherub
missing its face. Shuttered windows stare down from the great house, and
in one of them a curtain twitches as you look. The front door stands
north, studded with nails and painted a dead black, and the gate lies
back south.

1902.name: The Grand Foyer

north.description: To the north lies The Kitchen.

east.description: To the east lies The Living Room.

south.description: To the south lies The Front Yard.

west.description: To the west lies The Sitting Room.

up.description: To the up lies On The Grand Staircase.

down.description: To the down lies The Basement Laboratory.

1902.description:
A grand foyer rises two floors under a chandelier so thick with cobwebs
that it hangs like a great grey nest, and the black and white tiles
beneath are dull with dust. Family portraits climb the walls in heavy
frames, and their painted eyes follow you across the floor. A wide
staircase curves up to the gallery, and a low door beneath it leads down
to the cellar. Arches open north to the kitchen, east to the living room
and west to the sitting room, while the front door lies south.

extra_descs.portraits portrait:
The family stares down in oils: a stern father, a pale mother, three
children in Sunday dress, each face a little greyer than the last. Their
eyes are bright, and they never rest on the same place twice.

1903.name: The Sitting Room

north.description: To the north lies The Dining Room.

east.description: To the east lies The Grand Foyer.

west.description: To the west lies The Library.

1903.description:
A grand piano stands in the bay of this sitting room, its lid raised,
and every so often a few slow notes of a half-remembered waltz drift out
though no hands touch the keys. Moth-eaten armchairs face a cold
fireplace, and the wallpaper hangs in long damp tongues. A door west
leads to the library, an opening north gives onto the dining room, and
the foyer lies back east.

extra_descs.piano:
The ivory keys are yellow and chipped, and the dust on them lies in a
perfect, undisturbed layer. Yet when you are not looking, the hammers
sometimes stir.

1904.name: The Library

north.description: To the north lies The Hidden Staircase.

east.description: To the east lies The Sitting Room.

1904.description:
Shelves climb to the ceiling, bowed with crumbling books, and a rolling
ladder is stuck fast on its rail. Cold gathers in the corner by the
globe, and the pages of an open volume on the reading desk turn over
slowly, one at a time. A narrow door in the shelves to the north stands
ajar on a hidden stair, and the sitting room lies back east.

1905.name: The Living Room

west.description: To the west lies The Grand Foyer.

1905.description:
Sheeted furniture crowds the living room like patient ghosts, and a vast
stone hearth gapes cold behind a screen of rotting embroidery. Dust lies
thick on the mantel, broken only by the clear outline of a missing
clock. A faded carpet shows the track of a rocking chair that creaks in
the corner whenever you turn your back. The only way out is the wide
arch back west to the foyer.

1906.name: The Greenhouse

west.description: To the west lies The Kitchen.

1906.description:
Dead plants fill the greenhouse in brittle brown ranks, their clay pots
cracked and their leaves rattling at the slightest breath of air. Grimy
glass panes make a grey roof overhead, several of them broken, and a
bench of rotted seedling trays sags under a litter of dry soil. A vine
as thick as your wrist has strangled the iron frame, and its pale
blossoms are still faintly, wrongly, alive. The only way out is the
glass door west, back into the kitchen.

1907.name: The Kitchen

east.description: To the east lies The Greenhouse.

south.description: To the south lies The Grand Foyer.

west.description: To the west lies The Servants Corridor.

1907.description:
Cold iron pots hang from rusted hooks above a vast black range, and the
long table is scarred by a century of cleavers. A cold spot lingers by
the hearth, where the air bites at your fingers and a pot lid rattles
faintly on nothing. A glass door east opens on the greenhouse, the
servants' corridor runs on west, and the grand foyer lies south.

1908.name: The Servants Corridor

north.description: To the north lies The Housekeeper's Room.

east.description: To the east lies The Kitchen.

south.description: To the south lies The Cook's Room.

west.description: To the west lies The End Of The Servants Corridor.

1908.description:
A plain low corridor of whitewash and bare boards, where servants once
hurried unseen between the kitchen and the rooms off the passage. A
board of little brass bells hangs over the doors, each one labelled with
the name of a room, and now and then one trembles and rings with no hand
upon its wire. Doors open north and south, the kitchen lies back east,
and the corridor runs on west to its end.

1909.name: The End Of The Servants Corridor

north.description: To the north lies The Butler's Room.

east.description: To the east lies The Servants Corridor.

south.description: To the south lies The Chef's Room.

1909.description:
The corridor ends here at a blank wall hung with a single cracked
mirror, in which the whitewash looks greyer and the doors look farther
apart than they are. Doors stand north and south, and the passage runs
back east toward the kitchen. A smell of boiled cabbage and soap lingers
in the cold, and from the walls comes a soft knocking, like a hand
tapping to be let out.

1910.name: The Chef's Room

north.description: To the north lies The End Of The Servants Corridor.

east.description: To the east lies The Water Closet.

1910.description:
A chef's private room, smelling of old spices and rancid fat, with a
narrow bed, a cabinet of copper-bottomed pans and a tattered book of
recipes chained to the wall. Knife marks score the table, deep and many,
and a stain darkens the floorboards beneath it. The air is close and
oddly warm, as if a fire burned in the next room. A door east leads to a
water closet, and the way north returns to the end of the corridor.

1911.name: The Water Closet

east.description: To the east lies The Cook's Room.

west.description: To the west lies The Chef's Room.

1911.description:
This water closet is small and mean, whitewashed brick with a wooden
seat and a tin basin, built for the kitchen staff and not the family. A
rusted bucket stands in a corner, and a window no bigger than a book is
blocked with grime. The walls are scrawled with names and tallies in
pencil, some very old. A door east opens on the cook's room, and the
chef's room lies through the opening west.

1912.name: The Cook's Room

north.description: To the north lies The Servants Corridor.

west.description: To the west lies The Water Closet.

1912.description:
The cook's room is cramped and warm-smelling, hung with strings of dried
herbs gone to dust. A rocking chair sits before a little iron stove, and
an apron on a peg has a sooty handprint on its front that grows no
fainter however long you stare. The ticking of a clock fills the
silence, though there is no clock to be seen. A way north returns to the
servants' corridor, and the water closet lies west.

1913.name: The Housekeeper's Room

south.description: To the south lies The Servants Corridor.

west.description: To the west lies The Water Closet.

1913.description:
The housekeeper's room is tidy still, with a big ledger desk, a hook-
board of numbered keys and a narrow bed made up with a patched grey
quilt. A little window looks onto a blank wall, and the lamp on the desk
is full of oil though the wick is black. The cold is sharpest by the
bed, where the quilt keeps settling as if someone had just risen from
it. A door south leads back to the corridor, and an opening west gives
onto a water closet.

1914.name: The Water Closet

east.description: To the east lies The Housekeeper's Room.

west.description: To the west lies The Butler's Room.

1914.description:
A narrow water closet tiled in white and blue, the glaze crazed with age
and a long crack running down the basin. The pull chain swings gently
though the air is still, and water drips somewhere behind the wall in a
slow count. A door east leads back to the housekeeper's room, and an
opening west gives onto the butler's room. The smell of wet plaster is
thick here.

1915.name: The Butler's Room

east.description: To the east lies The Water Closet.

south.description: To the south lies The End Of The Servants Corridor.

1915.description:
The butler's room is a spare, upright place, with a tall narrow bed, a
wardrobe of black coats and a silver cabinet standing open and empty. A
plate-polishing board is propped against the wall, and a ring of old
stains on the table marks where a lamp or decanter long stood. Faint
footsteps cross the floor when you are still, pausing before the
wardrobe. A door east leads to the water closet, and the way south
returns to the end of the corridor.

1916.name: The Dining Room

south.description: To the south lies The Sitting Room.

1916.description:
A long table laid for twelve is furred with dust, every plate in its
place and every glass still holding a dark crust at the bottom. Candle
stubs burn low in the silver candelabra, though no one has lit them in
years. Chairs are pushed back at odd angles, as if the diners rose all
at once and fled. Only the doorway south to the sitting room breaks the
wall of dark panelling.

1917.name: On The Grand Staircase

up.description: To the up lies At The Top Of The Grand Staircase.

down.description: To the down lies The Grand Foyer.

1917.description:
The grand staircase sweeps up in a broad curve, its red carpet worn to
threads and its banister carved with climbing roses. A tall clock
halfway up has stopped at a quarter to three. Each step creaks beneath
your weight, and from above comes the soft tread of someone pacing,
which stops whenever you stop. The foyer lies down below, and the stair
climbs on to the upper landing.

1918.name: At The Top Of The Grand Staircase

east.description: To the east lies The Maid's Room.

south.description: To the south lies The Center Of The Hall.

west.description: To the west lies The Upstairs Water Closet.

down.description: To the down lies On The Grand Staircase.

1918.description:
The stair ends on a broad landing, where a tall window black with grime
looks over the dead garden. A long runner of faded carpet leads south
down the hall, and doors stand east and west, each with a tarnished
brass handle. Cold air pools around your ankles, and the banister seems
to hum faintly under your hand. The stair goes down to the foyer.

1919.name: The Center Of The Hall

north.description: To the north lies At The Top Of The Grand Staircase.

east.description: To the east lies The Master Bedroom.

south.description: To the south lies The End Of The Hall.

west.description: To the west lies A Little Girl's Room.

1919.description:
Portrait frames and closed doors line the walls of the hall, and the
runner underfoot is worn to the boards. A hopscotch grid is chalked on
the floorboards, the chalk fresh and white in the dust. The hall leads
north to the top of the great staircase and south to its far end, with a
door east to the master bedroom and another west to a child's room. A
faint giggle echoes down the corridor, then stops.

1920.name: The End Of The Hall

north.description: To the north lies The Center Of The Hall.

east.description: To the east lies The Sitting Room.

west.description: To the west lies The Guest Room.

1920.description:
The hall ends in a blank wall hung with a cracked mirror in which the
passage seems to run on longer than it does. Doors stand east and west,
and the hall runs back north toward its center. From the rafters
overhead comes the slow drag of something heavy across the boards, then
silence.

1921.name: The Upstairs Water Closet

east.description: To the east lies At The Top Of The Grand Staircase.

1921.description:
A cramped closet fitted with a porcelain basin and a mahogany seat, the
pull chain swinging a little in a draught that has no source. Cracked
tiles line the walls, and a tap drips with a slow, patient rhythm. The
mirror above the basin is fogged from the inside, and a finger has drawn
a small face in it. The door east leads back to the landing.

1922.name: The Maid's Room

south.description: To the south lies The Master Bedroom.

west.description: To the west lies At The Top Of The Grand Staircase.

1922.description:
A small plain room with a narrow iron cot, a washstand and a row of pegs
where black uniforms hang gone green with age. A mirror over the
washstand is draped in a cloth that has fallen off and been replaced
more than once. A connecting door south opens to the master bedroom, and
the way west leads back to the landing.

1923.name: A Little Girl's Room

east.description: To the east lies The Center Of The Hall.

1923.description:
Peeling pink wallpaper, a small bed under a lace canopy and a dolls'
house stand in this little girl's room, and a rocking horse faces the
window with its painted eyes cracked. A music box on the shelf chimes
thinly now and then, though its key is long gone. The air is cold and
smells of lavender and wax. The only way out is the door east to the
hall.

extra_descs.dolls house dollhouse:
The dolls' house is a perfect copy of the great house, down to the tiny
portraits in the foyer. A tiny figure stands in every room, and one
stands at the open window of the little girl's room, facing out.

1924.name: The Master Bedroom

north.description: To the north lies The Maid's Room.

south.description: To the south lies The Sitting Room.

west.description: To the west lies The Center Of The Hall.

1924.description:
A vast four-poster bed dominates the room, its curtains moth-eaten and
its mattress sunk in the middle as though someone were still lying
there. Above the mantel hangs a portrait of a husband and wife whose
smiles seem a little wider each time you look. A faint scent of lavender
water hangs on the cold air. The maid's room lies north, a door south
leads to a private sitting room, and an opening west gives onto the
hall.

1925.name: The Guest Room

east.description: To the east lies The End Of The Hall.

1925.description:
A guest room prepared for visitors who never arrived: sheets gone
yellow, a washbasin cracked from rim to base, a single candle stub in a
dish. The window is nailed shut from the inside, and the nails are
bright with fresh rust. A faint scratching comes from the wardrobe, and
stops when you listen. A door east leads back to the end of the hall.

1926.name: The Sitting Room

north.description: To the north lies The Master Bedroom.

west.description: To the west lies The End Of The Hall.

1926.description:
A lady's private sitting room, lit by a dusty rose glow from a small
stained-glass window, with a writing desk whose lock is broken, a faded
chaise and a spinning wheel with a snapped thread. The cold at the
window is so deep that the glass beads with moisture. Someone has been
sitting on the chaise recently, for the cushion is dented. A way north
returns to the master bedroom, and an opening west leads to the end of
the hall.

1927.name: The Hidden Staircase

south.description: To the south lies The Library.

down.description: To the down lies The Hidden Room.

1927.description:
Narrow steps spiral down behind the library shelves, and the walls are
close enough to brush both shoulders. Cobwebs hang in grey veils, parted
in the middle as though someone had passed this way not long ago. The
air is chill and still, with a faint smell of damp earth. A door south
leads back to the library, and the stair drops down to a hidden room.

1928.name: The Hidden Room

up.description: To the up lies The Hidden Staircase.

1928.description:
A small windowless chamber, bare but for a rotted table, a child's chair
and heaps of mouldering paper. Letters in a feminine hand are pinned
across the walls, scrawled over and over with the same few words. The
cold is deep, and your breath hangs before you. The stair climbs up to
the library above, and there is no other way out.

extra_descs.letters words:
The letters all begin 'Dearest' and end with the same few lines,
repeated until the paper is black: let me out, let me out, it is so cold
here.

1929.name: The Basement Laboratory

up.description: To the up lies The Grand Foyer.

1929.description:
Brick vaults arch overhead in this old laboratory, where long benches of
stained oak hold racks of glass, a rusted brass microscope and jars of
dark liquid. An iron table with leather straps stands in the middle of
the floor, its drain clogged with something black. The smell is of sour
chemicals and cold stone. Stairs climb up to the grand foyer, and a pale
green glimmer shifts in the jars when you move.

1930.name: The Main Gate to the Carnival

north.description: To the north lies The Main Carnival Grounds.

south.description: To the south lies The Eastern Gatehouse.

1930.description:
The carnival's main gate is a tall arch of painted wood, its gilt
letters flaking and its iron turnstiles rusted fast beneath it. Faded
bunting droops from the beams, and a ticket booth stands shuttered, its
glass cracked into a spider's web. Somewhere far off a calliope wheezes
a few notes and stops. The midway opens north among the stalls, and
behind you the road runs south toward the Eastern Gatehouse.

extra_descs.arch letters sign:
The gilt letters spell out a welcome to the finest carnival in the
realm, and beneath them, in a different hand and newer paint, someone
has added three words: we are waiting.

1931.name: The Main Carnival Grounds

north.description: To the north lies The Northern End of the Carnival.

east.description: To the east lies Hall of the Dancing Nymphs.

south.description: To the south lies The Main Gate to the Carnival.

west.description: To the west lies Sorcha the Seer of the Future, Teller of Fortunes.

1931.description:
The midway opens wide beneath a patchwork roof of rotting canvas, with
stalls on every side under ruined awnings and the sawdust trampled to a
grey crust. Faded paper lanterns sway on their wires without a breath of
wind. Paths lead north toward the far end of the grounds, east to a hall
hung with painted nymphs, west to a fortune-teller's booth, and south
back to the gate.

1932.name: The Northern End of the Carnival

north.description: To the north lies The Fiery Depths of Hades!.

east.description: To the east lies North-East End of the Carnival.

south.description: To the south lies The Main Carnival Grounds.

west.description: To the west lies Strongman Hall of Fame.

1932.description:
The midway narrows at this end into a lane of sagging booths, a ring-
toss stall with its hoops long gone and a coconut shy with a ragged
backdrop. Dried streamers hang from the canvas overhead, and a smell of
old sugar and mildew lingers. A red-painted entrance glows dimly ahead
to the north, a path runs east along the stalls, and west a broad hall
bears a painted sign. The main grounds lie back south.

1933.name: North-East End of the Carnival

north.description: To the north lies The Lair of the Two-Headed Tiger.

east.description: To the east lies Sammy the Stupendous Sword Swallower.

south.description: To the south lies The Eastern Carnival Grounds.

west.description: To the west lies The Northern End of the Carnival.

1933.description:
Here the grounds bend around a cluster of striped tents, their canvas
sagging and their ropes slack, the paint on their signs peeling away in
long curls. Trampled straw and dry mud cover the ground, and a lopsided
banner flaps in a draught. A path leads north to a caged lair, a tent
lies east with a swordsman's sign, the main walk runs south, and a lane
runs back west.

1934.name: Hall of the Dancing Nymphs

west.description: To the west lies The Main Carnival Grounds.

1934.description:
A round pavilion hung with painted nymphs who dance on the walls in a
ring, their pale arms linked among garlands of dead flowers. The paint
has peeled, and each nymph's face has gone blank as an egg. A little
stage in the centre holds a ring of tarnished lamps, and a thin, sweet
music seems to hum from nowhere. The way out is the curtained opening
west to the carnival grounds.

1935.name: Sorcha the Seer of the Future, Teller of Fortunes

east.description: To the east lies The Main Carnival Grounds.

1935.description:
Heavy purple drapes cover the walls of this little booth, and a round
table holds a crystal ball clouded like a cataract. Painted stars and
moons crowd the ceiling, and the cards painted on the wall show a hanged
man, a tower and a pale hand reaching from a cloud. The smell of incense
is sharp and bitter. The curtain opening east leads back to the carnival
grounds, and the table seems set for two.

1936.name: Strongman Hall of Fame

east.description: To the east lies The Northern End of the Carnival.

down.description: To the down lies Below the Carnival.

1936.description:
A long hall of faded glory, its walls hung with portraits of vast,
mustached strongmen and the iron dumbbells they hoisted. A tall high-
striker stands in one corner, its bell cracked and its painted gauge
worn down to the stub. The boards in the centre of the floor are scarred
where weights have been dropped, and a trapdoor with an iron ring stands
open to a stair leading down. The carnival lies east.

1937.name: The Fiery Depths of Hades!

south.description: To the south lies The Northern End of the Carnival.

1937.description:
This ride was built to look like the pit of hell, with black walls
streaked with painted flames and red glass lanterns hanging dark on iron
chains. A great demon's face of papier-mache gapes over the track, its
jaws full of cracked teeth, and a rusted rail vanishes into the gloom
behind it. The air is stale and tastes of tar and grease. The only way
out is back south to the Northern End of the Carnival.

1938.name: The Eastern Carnival Grounds

north.description: To the north lies North-East End of the Carnival.

east.description: To the east lies Sideshow Freaks.

south.description: To the south lies The Main Carnival Grounds.

1938.description:
Packed mud and scattered straw cover the ground between tattered tents
on this side of the carnival, and a long row of empty benches faces a
rickety stage. Glass bulbs on a string are dead along the edge of the
canvas roof, and a mildew-coated wheel of fortune stands still. A path
runs north toward the tents, east to a gaudy sideshow, and south to the
main grounds.

1939.name: The Lair of the Two-Headed Tiger

north.description: To the north lies The Tiger's Den.

south.description: To the south lies North-East End of the Carnival.

1939.description:
A great cage wagon stands open here, its iron bars bent outward in
places and thick with rust, and the floor is strewn with old straw gone
black. Deep claw marks score the planking in sets of two, and a heavy
musk still clings to the air. A painted board proclaims the beast within
as the wonder of the age, though much of the paint has gone. A hatch
north leads into the den, and the carnival lies south.

1940.name: Sammy the Stupendous Sword Swallower

west.description: To the west lies North-East End of the Carnival.

1940.description:
A small striped tent shelters a raised stage with a faded scarlet
curtain, and a rack of rusted swords stands upright in a stand beside
it. A painted board lists the swallower's daring feats in flaking
letters, and lamps with blackened chimneys line the footlights. Drifts
of dust cover the sawdust floor, with one bare patch where a man might
stand. The tent flap opens west to the carnival.

1941.name: Sideshow Freaks

west.description: To the west lies The Eastern Carnival Grounds.

1941.description:
A row of curtained alcoves lines this sideshow, each with a painted
banner hung above it that boasts of marvels long since vanished. The
curtains hang in motionless folds, and cracked mirrors in gilt frames
catch your reflection in odd, bent shapes. The air is close and hushed,
and faint whispers rise from behind the cloth when you step. The only
way out is west to the carnival grounds.

1942.name: The Tiger's Den

south.description: To the south lies The Lair of the Two-Headed Tiger.

1942.description:
The den is a low, dark box of planking at the back of the cage wagon,
lined with old straw and stinking of animal. Two great hollows are
pressed into the straw, side by side, where two heads once lay. Claws
have gouged the walls to splinters in long, desperate stripes. The only
way out is back south to the lair.

1943.name: Below the Carnival

east.description: To the east lies A Dank Passage.

up.description: To the up lies Strongman Hall of Fame.

1943.description:
A low cellar of earth and timber props stretches under the carnival,
damp and cold, the floor beaten into black mud. Rotting crates stack
against the supports, and the dim light from above shows only a few
broken planks and dripping beams. A stair climbs up to the Strongman
Hall of Fame, and a passage leads east into the dark.

1944.name: A Dank Passage

east.description: To the east lies The Fun-House of Nis!.

west.description: To the west lies Below the Carnival.

1944.description:
The passage is narrow and wet, its brick walls beaded with slime and its
low ceiling dripping into puddles on the floor. Rusted pipes run
overhead, and a smell of mould and stagnant water hangs heavy in the
dark. Somewhere ahead, faint and tinny, a music box plays a jolting
waltz. The passage runs east toward a painted doorway and west to the
cellar.

1945.name: The Fun-House of Nis!

east.description: To the east lies The Begining of the Fun House.

west.description: To the west lies A Dank Passage.

1945.description:
A huge painted face looms over the entrance to the fun-house, its mouth
gaping as a doorway and its laughing eyes crossed with cracks. Warped
mirrors line the walls on either side and bend you into long pale shapes
with stretched limbs. The floor tilts under your feet, and a giddy,
laughing music crackles from somewhere deeper in. The fun-house goes on
east, and a passage returns west.

extra_descs.mirrors mirror:
In every warped glass you stand taller and thinner than you are, and now
and then a second figure stands behind your shoulder, then vanishes as
you turn.

1946.name: The Begining of the Fun House

north.description: To the north lies A Collapsed Room.

south.description: To the south lies A Collapsed Room.

west.description: To the west lies The Fun-House of Nis!.

1946.description:
Here the floor slopes and the walls lean, the whole room built to tip
your balance, and a rotating barrel on its side blocks half the width.
Mirrors of every shape cover the ceiling, so that countless faces peer
down at you, all a little wrong. Plaster dust lies thick on the boards.
A doorway north leads to a fallen room, another south opens on another,
and the way west returns to the entrance.

1947.name: A Collapsed Room

south.description: To the south lies The Begining of the Fun House.

1947.description:
Half the ceiling has come down here in a fall of plaster, laths and
splintered beams, burying one side of the room under a long grey slope.
Painted stars on what remains of the roof show through the wreckage, and
a cracked clown's head lies grinning in the rubble. Dust stirs in the
still air. The only passable way is the doorway south to the entrance of
the fun-house.

1948.name: A Collapsed Room

north.description: To the north lies The Begining of the Fun House.

1948.description:
The floor of this room has given way in the middle, leaving a ragged pit
edged by broken joists and bent springs of the trick floor. Wallpaper in
red and gold stripes peels from the wall in strips, and the mirror on
the far side is a spiderweb of silver cracks. A chill breath rises out
of the gap. The only safe way out is the doorway north.
